claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA has a ductile FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure.
The as-cast alloy has a low or minimal degree of L12 ordering.
The as-cast alloy has relatively smooth or less serrated B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Aging between 550°C and 750°C induces L12 ordering and evolution of B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Aging for approximately 1–10 hours is typically sufficient to reach peak ordering in the stated temperature regime.
The brittle condition contains high-density L12 ordered domains within the FCC matrix.
The brittle condition contains jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Increasing L12 chemical ordering raises the antiphase-boundary energy.
Increasing L12 chemical ordering reduces the intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
High APBE and reduced SISFE restrict dislocation cross-slip and force planar slip arrays.
Planar slip bands interacting with jagged phase boundaries produce localized stress concentrations.
These localized stresses exceed the fracture toughness of the ordered matrix and cause brittle failure.
Aging above 750°C thermally disorders L12, lowers APBE, restores cross-slip, and thereby restores ductility.
Elongation reaches a minimum near 600°C, where L12 ordering is maximal.
Ductility recovers at 750°C because the degree of L12 ordering decreases.
The critical chemical-ordering boundary occurs when the L12 order parameter makes APBE exceed the energy barrier for cross-slip.
This critical ordering condition typically occurs when the FCC matrix approaches the stoichiometric Ni3Al ratio.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism place disordering and restored cross-slip above 750°C, whereas the predicted outcome says ductility has already recovered at 750°C. The transition temperature is therefore stated inconsistently.
